This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s).

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a557fa386bc3119379b1525bade763d00578396d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e4481e078fac7f477d361e4722d33274200fceeb` — the merge of head `8d546c802101bf50b4f94499473858a5f8f83fd7` into base `a557fa386bc3119379b1525bade763d00578396d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e4481e078fac7f477d361e4722d33274200fceeb && git checkout e4481e078fac7f477d361e4722d33274200fceeb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a557fa386bc3119379b1525bade763d00578396d 8d546c802101bf50b4f94499473858a5f8f83fd7 && git checkout -B drift-repro a557fa386bc3119379b1525bade763d00578396d && git merge --no-ff 8d546c802101bf50b4f94499473858a5f8f83fd7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a557fa386bc3119379b1525bade763d00578396d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs a557fa386bc3119379b1525bade763d00578396d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Seat ruling · #33703 (p1 #33651) · `Metadata-protocol:` · 2026-11-15T08:44Z · **A: `none`, patch.** (Independent Fable review of the facts and both options, per the pilot's ruling rule.)

- Nothing an author writes changes meaning or default (AGENTS.md's `semantic` definition): no key, value or default moves; only objectql internals change.
- The author-facing async texts are `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts:559` ("runs in the background and does not block the transaction") and `skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md:64` ("in the background, after commit"). This PR makes them true: async after-hook writes are now stored when a blocking hook shares the event or a caller transaction is open (before, they were lost).
- The old "rolls back with the trigger" outcome for async hooks was timing-dependent and already false after #22855, so it was never a contract.
- The `HookEvent` docblock at `hook.zod.ts:353-355` ("`ctx.api` / `ctx.ql` writes join the same transaction and roll back with everything else") is unqualified and reads as covering async hooks too. It should say "blocking hooks only". That is a prose correction on a governed spec surface, so it is a separate follow-up card (filed after the drain), not part of this objectql patch.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `58f6cf7d81e604d906320b4fa9252a335c98e14e`
Local-runs: none

The PR's file list is the changeset, `unit-detach.ts` (new), `engine.ts`, `engine-scoped-context.ts`, `engine-transactions-section.ts`, `hook-wrappers.ts` and two test files, all in `packages/objectql`. It has no published schema and no governed path, and the changeset declares `Clause-②: no`. So this is a plain review record with no ④. The head adds only a merge of `origin/main` (412fbf76) over `35d7a01a` and touches no file of this diff.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The detach is correct, and only async hooks get it.** `runDetachedHook` is called on one site only, the `fireAndForget` branch of `wrapDeclarativeHook`. The awaited path (`await runWithErrorPolicy(ctx)`) is unchanged, so blocking hooks and their `ctx.api` writes still join the door's or the caller's unit and roll back with it. The `blocking only` control and the blocking leg's enrolled write in the first repro test (`noteUnenrolled` = `[false, true]`) pin this.
- **Both ways a handle reaches the hook are cut.** Ambient: `AsyncLocalStorage#exit` on the engine's `txStore`, and the continuations the hook body creates inherit the empty store. Explicit: the ambient handle and the handle the hook's `ctx.api` carries are recorded in a second `AsyncLocalStorage`, and `isClosedUnitHandle` answers `true` for them. Every reader of a threaded handle I found goes through that predicate: `buildDriverOptions`, `opensAfterAbortUnit`, the secret-row release and `openTransactionKind`. A unit the hook opens itself gets a fresh handle. The memory, mongodb and sql drivers each return a new object per `beginTransaction`, so a hook's own unit is never mistaken for a detached one. Nested detached runs add to the set.
- **Identity and tenant scope are kept.** The detach touches only the `transaction` facet. It runs on `detached.api`, which is the `runAs`-derived api when there is one (#14010, #25653), and the execution context's user, tenant and `isSystem` are not read or rewritten. Only `txStore` is exited. The cascade stores (`cascadeDeleteSets`, `cascadeIssuedDeletes`) still propagate, as before. No privilege is gained or lost.
- **Errors are still handled.** The detached promise keeps its `.then(recordOutcome).catch(log)` chain, and `runWithErrorPolicy` is async, so a throw in the hook becomes a rejection that the chain catches. No unhandled rejection is added.
- **The symbol-count pin is legitimate.** `[DETACHED_HOOK_RUN]` is a real third symbol-keyed member of `ScopedContext.prototype`, and the pin also asserts that the package entry does not export it (`'DETACHED_HOOK_RUN' in entry === false`), as it does for the other two. Nothing is hidden.
- **must-fix: the hook still starts before the triggering unit commits, and the changeset does not say so.** The PR's own first repro test shows it: the async hook's `note` write reaches the driver unenrolled while the blocking leg is still running inside the door's unit, so before the unit commits. On a database with more than one connection (Postgres, MySQL, Mongo), the hook's `ctx.api` reads and writes on their own connection therefore see the state from before the triggering write until that unit commits. Examples: an `async afterUpdate` that re-reads its record can read the old values, and an `async afterInsert` that updates the new row or inserts a child that references it can find no row. Before this PR, the same early statements joined the unit and saw the write. The changeset says the writes run "as they would with no unit open". That is true for enrolment but not for what they see: with no unit open, the triggering write is already committed. The seat ruling (6891864249) also says this PR makes `data-hooks.md:64` ("in the background, after commit") true, and it does not: the hook runs in the background, but not after commit. Fix: add one bullet to the changeset and the PR body, for example: "An async hook can start before the triggering write's unit commits. On a database with more than one connection, its reads and writes do not see that write until the unit commits." Deferring async dispatch until the unit settles is the alternative that would make "after commit" true. That is a design choice for the seat, not a requirement of this record.
- nit: `ScopedContext#transactionHandle` and the nested `HookContext.transaction` (`engine-insert.ts:634` and the update, delete and find twins) still expose the detached handle as a raw value inside the detached run. A hook that passes it to a driver by hand gets the closed unit. This was already so after #22855 and is not new here.

### ② Semver level

**Clause-② ruling: `no`, as declared.** No answer to the triggering request moves, because nothing waits for an async hook. The hook's own writes go from lost ("Transaction query already complete") to stored, and that adds side effects, not refusals. Early writes no longer roll back with the trigger, which the changeset declares. Early reads now see the state from before the trigger on multi-connection databases. Like the rollback outcome, what an early statement saw depended on timing before this PR too, and late statements have run unenrolled before commit since #22855. So it is no contract move. It does need to be declared (①).

**`Metadata-protocol: none` stands** (seat 5, 6891864249): no authorable key, value or default changes. `@objectstack/objectql: patch`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The spec prose follow-up seat 5 named (`hook.zod.ts:353-355`, "blocking hooks only") is outside this PR. The same follow-up should also correct `data-hooks.md:64` "after commit", unless dispatch is deferred.
- There is no real-driver (knex/Postgres) twin for the new path. The author declares this. The visibility point in ① is the case such a twin would show.
- CI at this head when read (09:28Z): 35 success, 18 skipped, `Test Core (1/8)` in progress, none red.
- The PR is a draft.

domain:server#6 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4cztR1A2CZoxSZyuoGP

Seat ruling amendment · #33703 (p1 #33651) · 2026-11-15T09:30Z · amends 6891864249 after review#3 FAIL 6892346943. **Option (a): declare the gap, text only.**

- review#3 is right: the detach fixes the lost writes ("Transaction query already complete"), but an async after-hook still starts before the triggering unit commits. On Postgres, MySQL and Mongo it can read the pre-write state, and if the unit rolls back the hook has already run. My earlier premise that this PR makes "after commit" true does not hold, and that bullet is withdrawn.
- objectql's transaction unit has no general commit-callback registry today (the only `onCommit` is the batch-data response builder in metadata-protocol), so after-commit dispatch is new mechanism with new pins and a real-driver twin. That does not belong in a p1 correctness patch.
- In this PR: the changeset and PR body say plainly that async after-hooks run in the background but are not deferred to commit (they may observe pre-commit state and are not cancelled on rollback). `skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md:64` drops "after commit" and says the same.
- `Metadata-protocol: none`, patch, stands: no authorable key, value or default changes.
- Follow-up p2 card (E2b files it): queue async after-hooks on the unit, run on commit, drop on rollback. That card also owns the `hook.zod.ts:353-355` and `hook.zod.ts:559` prose.
- Land after a review#3 text delta on the new head.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `8d546c802101bf50b4f94499473858a5f8f83fd7`
Local-runs: none

This is a delta over FAIL 6892346943 at `58f6cf7d`. `git diff 58f6cf7d..8d546c80` touches one file, `.changeset/33651-async-hook-outside-door-unit.md` (2 lines added, 1 removed). `8da0a761` also edited `skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md`, and `8d546c80` reverted that edit, so no skills/** path is in the net diff. No source or test file moved, so the code judgments of 6892346943 ① carry unchanged. The changeset still declares `Clause-②: no`, so this is a plain review record with no ④.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The must-fix of 6892346943 is met.** The changeset's new first bullet and the PR body's "Update at 8d546c80" section say the gap plainly, and each part matches the code. First, the hook starts at dispatch, which can be before the triggering unit commits: `runDetachedHook` runs it at once on the fire-and-forget leg of `wrapDeclarativeHook`, and nothing queues it on the unit. Second, on a database with more than one connection, its `ctx.api` reads and writes run on their own connection, so they do not see the triggering write until that write commits. The afterUpdate re-read and afterInsert child-row examples are the cases I raised. Third, the hook is not cancelled when the unit rolls back, because no code path cancels it. The SQLite bullet, which says the hook's write waits for the connection, is consistent with this.
- **The "as with no unit open" sentence is now limited to enrolment.** It reads "enrolled in no unit and run on their own connection, as they would with no unit open", and the next sentence says what the hook sees differs, with a pointer to the first bullet. Nothing claims "after commit" any more. The bullet's advice ("should be a blocking hook instead") matches the existing rollback bullet's advice.
- **The text matches the seat's amendment as narrowed.** Amendment 6892365442 is option (a): declare the gap, text only. Seat note 6892475527 moves the `data-hooks.md:64` rewording out of this PR into #33760. Both are followed: the changeset and the body declare the gap, and the skills reference is untouched.
- **The follow-up exists and covers what moved.** #33760 is open with `priority:p2`. It is the after-commit dispatch card ("queue async after-hooks on the unit, run on commit, drop on rollback", with pins and a real-driver twin), and it owns `data-hooks.md:64` "in the background, after commit", plus the `hook.zod.ts:353-355` and `:559` prose. There is no second card. #33760 is both the dispatch card and the prose card.
- nit: the bullet says that before this change those early statements "joined the unit, saw the write, and failed or rolled back with it". It leaves out the third outcome: a statement that finished before the unit committed was stored with it. This is not misleading about the change.
- nit: the PR body's 维护者速读 "风险与回滚" line names the rollback change but not the visibility gap. The body's update section and the changeset carry the gap, so nothing in the body is stale or contradicted. The acceptance note "Flagged for the seat" is superseded by #33760, which the update section names.

### ② Semver level

**Clause-② ruling: `no`, as declared, unchanged from 6892346943.** The delta is changelog text only. **`Metadata-protocol: none`** stands (6891864249, 6892365442, 6892475527). `@objectstack/objectql: patch`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Until #33760 lands, `data-hooks.md:64` still says "after commit", which is untrue. The seat accepted this in 6892475527.
- There is still no real-driver twin for the detached path. #33760's acceptance asks for one.

- The PR is a draft.
